In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, fabrication, and characterization of polyelectrophilic multilayer systems with a natural glycosamino glycan, heparin, and semisynthetic polysaccharides, CS, as polyanions.
fabrication of multilayers with heparin and CS blends and their interactions with C2C 12 cells.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
heparin, due to its unique chemical structure, was preferentially incorporated into blend multilayers and dominated the biological interactions.
multilayers with heparin and CS2.6 were more hydrophobic and less hydrated compared to multilayers with CS1.6 and heparin.
heparin and CS2.6 blend systems are more hydrophilic and more hydrated as compared to CS1.6 blends and heparin multilayers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the blend multilayer films of heparin with CS2.6 and CS1.6 are promising candidates to be explored for biomedical applications such as tissue engineering.
heparin can be used as a model to understand the interactions between natural polysaccharides and semisynthetic polysaccharides with chitosan.
heparin and CS can be used together in blend multilayers to achieve a desired biological response. © 2018, The Author(s).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the multilayer growth and biological responses of the multilayers can be modulated by blending heparins with CS.
the physico-chemical and biological properties of polyelectrolite multilayers can be tuned by blending polyanionic components with distinct chemical and biological functionalities.
